name: Yoncalla
confidence_why: The only statement on Yoncalla stress is a passing remark in Hajda 1976, working from Frachtenberg's and Jacobs's unpublished notes on a language extinct since the 1930s, that stress is "often shifted to prefixed elements" unlike stem-initial Mary's River, and nothing else read (Lewis 2003, Hale 1846, Frachtenberg 1918, Zenk 1976, or the WALS entry from Berman 1990, which covers Central Kalapuya rather than Yoncalla) says anything about Yoncalla stress.
catalog_citation: Hajda, Yvonne P. 1976. Mary's River Kalapuyan: A Descriptive Phonology. MA thesis, Portland State University (PDXScholar ETD 2491, doi:10.15760/etd.2488). 72 pp. Corroborated by Hajda, Yvonne. 1976. The Phonemes of Mary's River Kalapuyan: Analyzing an Extinct Language. Papers for the 11th International Conference on Salish Languages (ICSNL 11), UBC Working Papers in Linguistics. 13 pp.
catalog_locator: Thesis: p.45, section 'Suprasegmentals'; summary sentence p.49 (p.57; 'Phonemic stress occurs on the first syllable of stems, and is accompanied by higher (or perhaps sometimes by lower) pitch'); printed = pdf - 8. Second published locus, same clause: Hajda 1976 ICSNL 11 paper, 'Stress' section p.10
catalog_quote: Frachtenberg occasionally does not mark stress, but he is remarkably consistent when he does show it. It occurs on both short and long vowels, and is thus independent of length, even though in at least one case (/ai/) it conditions length, and even though long vowels are more often stressed than unstressed. In Mary's River, it falls on the first syllable of a stem; in Tualatin and Yoncalla, stress is often shifted to prefixed elements. If a prefix is added in Mary's River, stress does not move: wau·tso?, kuwau·tso?. Stress is accompanied generally by higher pitch (sometimes perhaps by lower pitch), which Jacobs calls "pitch accent." He says that pitch accent falls on "every syllable felt to be an independent root--nominal, pronominal, connective, or verbal" (1930: n.p.). Since stress is not always predictable from the segmental construction alone, it is considered to be phonemic.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: The family pattern (explicit for Mary's River / Central Kalapuya, and coded 'initial' by WALS from Berman 1990) is a pitch accent/stress on the first syllable of the stem, unmoved by prefixation. For Yoncalla the only statement is a one-clause aside: stress is 'often shifted to prefixed elements', i.e. it does not stay on the stem-initial syllable but frequently lands on a prefix. No positional rule (initial, penultimate, etc.) is given for Yoncalla itself.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Yoncalla; 'often' implies the shift is not categorical.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (prefix+stem complexes), based on Frachtenberg's transcriptions and slip files; Hajda's own object is Mary's River, and the Yoncalla remark is comparative. Jacobs's 'pitch accent on every independent root' statement is family-general from an unpublished sketch.
new_statements.identity_note: Yoncalla = Southern Kalapuya (yonc1234, ISO sxk), distinct from Central Kalapuya (kala1400/kyl; Santiam, Mary's River) and Northern Kalapuya/Tualatin (tual1242/nrt). Hajda's Yoncalla data come via Frachtenberg's 1914 Grand Ronde notebook (Mrs Robert Allen, Mrs Tom Jackson) and slip files; Jacobs's 1928 Yonkalla data are from Laura Blackerty Albertson. The WALS 'Kalapuya' (klp) stress values are for Central Kalapuya, not Yoncalla.

sources.citation: Lewis, J. William. 2003. Central Kalapuya phonology: the segmental inventory of John Hudson's Santiam. MA thesis, University of Victoria. 319 pp.
sources.note: Central Kalapuya (Santiam) only: accent 'always predictable as being on the left-most syllabic nucleus of the root' (p.3; p.63 fn.14); p.152 cites Jacobs ca.1930:46 that the pitch accent on the left-most root vowel rises about three notes. On Yoncalla: p.20 fn.23 'I am not familar with Yonkalla (SK) to comment on its prefixal system'; p.117 fn.53 discusses geminates in Jacobs nb45 Yonkalla data; App. V p.284 notes Laura Blackerty Albertson could give no texts. No Yoncalla stress statement.
